text: Holding E to patch 'core: rotting' mid-slope (17 m below 0.4) let the boulder roll back down to the terrace below (now 28 m): the HUD offered 'Hold E to patch' while pushing with no warning that letting go of W drops the boulder. Expected either the patch prompt to warn, or patching to be disallowed off-terrace.

After the boulder rolled back to the 0.3 terrace, getting back below it and pushing it up again took ~10 minutes of wall clock: holding W toward it repeatedly slid me past it or up the valley side ('The boulder: 25 m behind you') with the release distance stuck at 28 m. There is no indicator of which way is uphill/the path, and the third-person camera hides the boulder when you are right next to it. Expected a clear 'get below it' cue or a direction arrow.

With 4 open issues the issue list reaches the crosshair row (y~178) and in-world module labels ('billing') draw over the help bar and the patch prompt text; the crosshair and prompt become hard to read.

On the 0.4 terrace the 'ui' issue label sits at the boulder's contact point with the ground: in first person the label is visible but the crosshair can't target it (prompt says 'Face the boulder and walk into it'). Fixing it requires rolling the boulder back from the uphill side, which costs a lot of positioning time.

When ui hit 0% (DOWN) the HUD showed 'OUTAGE: users are leaving' and Weight 'heavy' with the hint '(rot and modules weigh it down: patch, or retire,' which is cut off at the right edge of the 640px window. Issue list also grows past the crosshair ('... and 1 more' overlaps the prompt).

At 0.5 with 11 modules and 9 open issues (router and ui DOWN) the weight bar maxed out: 'too heavy to push uphill'. Pushing 25 s of game time moved the boulder backward (15 m -> 18 m). Issues spawned faster than one player could find and patch them (5 new issues between 0.4 and 0.5), so the climb stalled at 0.5 of 1.0.
Sitting (Q) on the 0.5 terrace hides the HUD and shows 'The boulder is still. For a moment, so are you.' over a quiet valley view: a lovely, calm beat even mid-outage.
